title: EU EV Battery Recycling Outlook 2026 (Nordwell Research)
text:
1. Summary
The EU-27 market for recycling lithium-ion batteries from electric vehicles generated EUR 1.9 billion of revenue in 2025, up from EUR 1.6 billion in 2024 (+19%). We forecast EUR 2.3 billion for 2026 and a compound annual growth rate of 21% from 2025 to 2030, reaching about EUR 4.9 billion in 2030.

2. Scope and method
The market is defined as revenue earned by companies for collection, logistics, discharging and dismantling, mechanical pre-treatment to black mass, and hydrometallurgical refining of EV and EV-production lithium-ion batteries inside the EU-27. Portable and industrial batteries are excluded. The resale value of recovered metals is not added to revenue: where recyclers sell black mass or metal salts, only the processing margin is counted, to avoid double counting with the metals market. Figures are in nominal euros and come from company filings for 23 operators plus interviews.

3. Drivers
Production scrap from EU gigafactories supplied about three quarters of 2025 feedstock. End-of-life packs are a minority until after 2030. The recycling efficiency and material recovery targets of Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 support investment in refining capacity.

4. Risks
Low lithium and nickel prices in 2024-2025 squeezed recyclers that depend on metal sales. Several announced refining projects were delayed. A slower EV ramp-up in Europe would cut production scrap, the main feedstock, and lower our growth forecast by up to 5 percentage points.
